children: Bank strike from September 28-30 may affect branch services, while UPI, ATMs and digital banking are expected to continue

Bank customers could face disruption in branch-based services from September 28 to 30 as the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) plans a three-day nationwide strike over the demand for a five-day banking week.

The action follows a September 11 one-day strike and comes just before the September 30 half-yearly closing of banks, making the period particularly significant for businesses and time-sensitive banking transactions.

The proposed strike has raised concerns over a longer disruption because September 26 is the fourth Saturday and September 27 is Sunday. However, the Finance Ministry said on September 23 that all public sector banks and regional rural banks will remain operational on Sunday, September 27, with RBI approval for bank branches, offices, ATM-linked branches and currency chests to function that day.

State Bank of India, Canara Bank and other public sector lenders have advised customers to complete important branch-related transactions before September 28. SBI has asked customers to use ATMs, Automated Deposit and Withdrawal Machines, Customer Service Points, YONO, internet and mobile banking and UPI during the strike period. Canara Bank has similarly advised customers to plan branch requirements in advance and use digital and self-service channels.

Services requiring physical documentation, employee assistance or branch processing could face delays if employees participate in the strike. Cheque-related processing and certain corporate banking activities may also be affected, particularly around the September 30 half-yearly closing.
UPI, ATMs And Digital Banking To Continue

The strike is not expected to shut down digital banking channels. Customers can continue using UPI, internet banking, mobile banking and bank-specific applications for routine transactions, while ATMs and other self-service machines are expected to remain operational.

The government has also taken steps to reduce the impact of the strike by opening public sector and regional rural bank branches on September 27. The move is intended to provide customers an additional banking day before the three-day strike begins.

The immediate dispute centres on the implementation of a five-day banking week. The government has said the Performance Linked Incentive (PLI) issue has been kept in abeyance, while the five-day workweek remains under consideration.

UFBU has maintained that it will proceed with the September 28-30 strike unless there is concrete progress on the demand. The unions have also proposed an indefinite nationwide strike from October 26 if the issue remains unresolved.
